categories.main_business_segments: Owens Corning operates four main business segments: Roofing, Insulation, Doors, and Composites. Roofing focuses on asphalt shingles and roofing components; Insulation covers thermal and acoustical products for residential, commercial, and industrial use; Doors (added via the Masonite acquisition in 2024) includes interior and exterior doors and door systems; and Composites manufactures glass fiber reinforcements and related products. The company is in the process of divesting its global glass reinforcements business and will reorganize into three segments post-divestiture.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages material science and manufacturing expertise, particularly in glass fiber technology, asphalt processing, and advanced insulation materials. Production methods include vertically integrated manufacturing for asphalt shingles, glass fiber reinforcement, and foam insulation, as well as continuous and batch processes for various building materials. Owens Corning emphasizes innovation in energy efficiency, sustainability, and product durability, supported by a robust intellectual property portfolio.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Owens Corning serves distributors, home centers, lumberyards, contractors, homebuilders, and retailers, with key end markets in residential and commercial construction, repair and remodeling, and industrial applications. Major customer concentration exists, with two customers accounting for 13% and 11% of 2024 net sales. The company’s products are used in new construction, repair/remodeling, and a wide range of industrial and infrastructure projects.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates globally, with significant presence in North America (especially the United States), Europe, Asia-Pacific, and Latin America. As of December 31, 2024, Owens Corning had 152 manufacturing facilities in 31 countries, with the majority of sales and operations concentrated in the U.S., Canada, and Europe. The company is strategically shifting focus toward North America and Europe, including divestitures in Asia-Pacific.
categories.supply_chain_position: Owens Corning is primarily a vertically integrated manufacturer, operating downstream in the supply chain by producing finished building materials and systems for direct sale to distributors, retailers, and contractors. In some cases, such as asphalt processing and glass fiber production, the company also supplies intermediate materials to other manufacturers, including internal use for its own products.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding branded building products, driving material innovation, and advancing sustainability initiatives (notably 2030 Sustainability Goals for energy, water, waste, and emissions reduction). R&D focuses on product performance, energy efficiency, recycled content, and reducing environmental impact. The company is reshaping its portfolio through acquisitions (e.g., Masonite) and divestitures (e.g., glass reinforcements) to align with its focus on building products in core geographies.
categories.revenue_model: Owens Corning generates revenue primarily through the sale of manufactured products—roofing shingles, insulation, doors, and composites—on a point-in-time basis when control transfers to customers. Additional revenue streams include extended warranties (recognized over time), processed asphalt sales, and, to a lesser extent, licensing and service agreements. The company does not rely on long-term volume contracts, with most sales based on short-term purchase orders.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Owens Corning is a market leader in North America for residential, commercial, and industrial fiberglass insulation, and is the second largest producer of asphalt roofing shingles in the U.S. Key competitors include other major building materials manufacturers such as CertainTeed, GAF, Johns Manville, and international glass fiber and insulation producers. The company competes on innovation, quality, service, and sustainability, and is recognized for its strong brands and broad product portfolio.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, Owens Corning reported net sales of $11.0 billion and net earnings of $647 million, with approximately 25,000 employees worldwide. The company completed the $3.2 billion acquisition of Masonite, expanding its scale and product offerings. While net earnings declined year-over-year due to one-time charges and restructuring, adjusted EBIT grew to $2.0 billion, reflecting underlying operational strength. The company maintains a robust balance sheet, with $5.1 billion in total debt post-acquisition.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Owens Corning differentiates itself through material innovation, sustainability leadership, and strong, trusted brands (e.g., PINK insulation, FOAMULAR, Masonite doors). The company emphasizes energy efficiency, product durability, and environmental stewardship, aiming to deliver superior performance and value to customers. Its vertically integrated operations, broad geographic reach, and commitment to continuous improvement in safety and sustainability further enhance its competitive positioning.
